payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Change the image into pencil drawing
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Compared with the source, is the image rendered pervasively as a pencil drawing, or is there perceptible but incomplete pencil-like treatment?
node.criteria: Pass only if the scene as a whole is clearly and pervasively rendered as a pencil drawing, with visible pencil-like linework and shading representing the scene. Fail if there is no perceptible change toward pencil drawing; muted color or grain alone does not establish progress. If there is perceptible pencil-like treatment but it is incomplete or the scene remains substantially photographic, fail this condition because the required whole-scene transformation is not satisfied. Use unknown only when visual evidence is genuinely insufficient to determine whether the required transformation is satisfied.
node.binding: Compare the supplied source image with the edited image. Assess visible evidence of actual pencil-like marks and shading across the scene. Require pervasive whole-scene pencil rendering for pass. Perceptible but incomplete pencil-like treatment does not satisfy this condition; muted color or grain alone is not evidence of progress. Reserve unknown for genuinely insufficient visual evidence.

node_traces.evidence: The edited image is muted and grainy, but the objects retain largely photographic textures and smooth tonal transitions. There is no pervasive visible pencil-like linework and shading across the scene, so the required whole-scene pencil drawing transformation is not satisfied.

response.content: {"text":"The node’s all-or-nothing criterion collapses the rubric’s distinction between “no progress” and “partial”: its trace explicitly notes a changed, muted/grainy image, yet concludes “no” solely because pencil rendering is not pervasive. Keep pervasive whole-scene rendering as the completion threshold, but make the decision separately assess whether there is perceptible pencil-like treatment versus merely color desaturation or grain, and map incomplete genuine treatment to partial rather than no. In these images, the edit visibly changes the source and adds a pale, textured, sketch-like appearance, while much of the scene still reads as photographic; investigate whether those marks are actual pencil-like treatment rather than treating incompleteness itself as evidence of no progress. Record evidence for both progress and remaining photographic areas, and calibrate confidence to that distinction. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is indicated."}
